problem.explanation: WHERE removes rows that fail either condition before SELECT returns id and name. ORDER BY makes the result deterministic. A common mistake is using OR, which includes inactive or old users. A composite index may help when this filter is common.
hints: Both the activity flag and signup date belong in WHERE.
Compare the date with a PostgreSQL DATE literal and combine conditions with AND.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE active = true AND signup_date >= DATE '2026-01-01' ORDER BY id;

problem.statement_markdown: Return id and name for active users who signed up on or after 2026-01-01. Sort by id.
